body: ## Bug Description After queueing a composer message in session A (turn running), switching to a brand-new chat showed **1 Queued** with session A's entry in the new chat's queue panel. The stored binding is correct — the entry later drained into session A, not the new chat — so this is a display-scope leak only, but while displayed it reads as "my message will fire into the wrong conversation". ## Steps to Reproduce 1. In desktop session A with a running turn, type a message and send → it queues ("1 Queued" appears). 2. Open a new chat (empty transcript). 3. The new chat's queue panel shows session A's queued entry (screenshot below). Storage inspection shows the entry is keyed under session A (see Root Cause Analysis). ## Expected Behavior A new chat shows an empty queue panel regardless of what other sessions have queued. ## Actual Behavior The previous session's queued prompt is displayed in the new chat's queue panel. Display-only: the entry drained into the correct session afterwards. ## Affected Component Other — Hermes Desktop (Electron app, packaged build). No "Desktop" entry exists in the dropdown. ## Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) N/A (desktop, local backend) ## Debug Report Same system dump as the companion clarify report #139189: `0.22.1+33.gca069e1 [ca069e12] (2026-10-14)`, Linux 7.2.10-200.fc44.x86_64, python 3.14.7, packaged desktop build. ## Operating System Fedora Linux 44 (Workstation Edition), kernel 7.2.10-200.fc44.x86_64, GNOME Wayland ## Python Version 3.14.7 ## Hermes Version 0.22.1+33.gca069e1 [ca069e12] (2026-10-14); desktop app footer shows v0.22.1+33 ## Root Cause Analysis (optional) Verified (renderer localStorage + state.db): - The queue store (`localStorage` key `hermes.desktop.composerQueue.v1`) held the entry under session A's own key (`local-7d7bc5b0e1dbe6ac…`): `{"id":"d3b61ad2…","text":"[queued prompt]","attachments":[],"queuedAt":…}` — binding correct. - After session A's turn ended (manual stop of a parked clarify turn), the entry drained into session A as the next user message (state.db row 95354, 22:05:28) — data-layer routing correct end to end. Only the display leaked. Suspected path (unverified — no CDP port on the packaged renderer): `activeQueueSessionKey = queueSessionKey || sessionId || freshDraftKey` (`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/index.tsx`). On a new-chat route `primaryRouteSelectedSessionId` returns `null` (the #59305 fix made the route authoritative over the store selection), so the key falls through to the `sessionId` prop; if that prop still holds the previous session's id during/after the switch, `useSessionSlice($queuedPromptsBySession, key)` selects the previous session's queue. An alternative candidate is the route flipping a frame behind the view. ## Deduplication - #59305 (closed) — cross-tab message mixing; its fix made the route authoritative for the composer scope key. This report is the residual fall-through branch (key resolves to `null` on a new-chat route) — same area, different branch. - Open PRs #131423 / #99795 / #66270 — adjacent session-switch state leaks (bound send across switches, leftover steer runtime, new-session window remembered routes); none covers the queue panel slice. - #123532 / #134096 / #130405 — queue content/projection issues, not cross-session display. --- Previous session New session

body: ## Bug Description A pending single-question `clarify` card disappeared from the desktop transcript with no user action, while the gateway-side request stayed pending. From then on the turn was unanswerable: the call site rendered **Result unavailable**, typed composer text went to the queue (turn still "running"), and the turn sat parked — turn lease alive, zero API calls — until the user force-stopped it 21 minutes later. Without the stop it would have waited up to the default 3600 s clarify timeout (`tools/clarify_gateway.py`). Storage stayed consistent throughout: one call row (assistant `tool_calls`), no result row while parked, one result row with `outcome: "cancelled"` after the stop. The disappearance is renderer-only; the gateway behaved correctly end to end. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. In a desktop session, have the agent issue a `clarify` call (single question with choices). 2. Switch to another session, then back, before answering. 3. The card is gone; the call site shows **Result unavailable**; the status bar still shows the turn running. There is no way to answer. (Observed 2026-10-15; the exact unmount trigger is not yet pinned down — see Root Cause Analysis.) ## Expected Behavior A pending clarify card survives session switches (or is re-armed on re-entry) and stays answerable until answered, skipped, or timed out. A human-input call whose result has legitimately not arrived yet never renders as a failed "Result unavailable". ## Actual Behavior The card unmounted by itself; the renderer fell back to the generic unavailable placeholder for a call still legitimately waiting on the user. The turn stranded for 21 min 19 s until manually stopped — `tool clarify completed (1278.99s)` shows the gateway-side request was alive the whole time. Timeline (state.db + agent.log, session `local-7d7bc5b0e1dbe6ac…`): - 21:44:08 — assistant row 95277 ends with `clarify` call `clarify_50_deb0ef0b` (1 question, 3 choices); this is API call #45 and the last API call of the turn. - 21:44 → 22:05 — `session_turn_leases` stays held and keeps refreshing; no API call in agent.log; card gone from the UI (screenshot below). - 22:05:28 — user stops the turn. Result row 95352 lands: `outcome: "cancelled"`, `status: "unanswered"`. Queued composer text drains in order as the next user turn (row 95354) and work resumes. ## Affected Component Other — Hermes Desktop (Electron app, packaged build). No "Desktop" entry exists in the dropdown. ## Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) N/A (desktop, local backend) ## Debug Report `hermes debug share --local` (system dump; raw log tail omitted — it contains unrelated private session content; filtered excerpts below and more available on request): ```text version: 0.22.1+33.gca069e1 [ca069e12] (2026-10-14) os: Linux 7.2.10-200.fc44.x86_64 x86_64 python: 3.14.7 openai_sdk: 2.24.0 profile: default model: ark-code-latest provider: ark-agent-plan terminal: local gateway: running (systemd (user), pid 2810) platforms: feishu, weixin ``` ## Operating System Fedora Linux 44 (Workstation Edition), kernel 7.2.10-200.fc44.x86_64, GNOME Wayland ## Python Version 3.14.7 ## Hermes Version 0.22.1+33.gca069e1 [ca069e12] (2026-10-14); desktop app footer shows v0.22.1+33 (packaged build, renderer has no CDP port) ## Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) agent.log around the stop (session `local-7d7bc5b0…`; message text redacted): ```text 22:05:28,003 agent.tool_executor: tool clarify completed (1278.99s, 380 chars) 22:05:28,041 agent.conversation_loop: Turn ended: reason=interrupted_by_user model=ark-code-latest api_calls=4/200 tool_turns=44 response_len=0 22:05:28,243 gateway.run: inbound message: platform=local … msg='[queued prompt]' ``` Last API call before the park — nothing follows until the stop: ```text 21:44:08,992 agent.conversation_loop: API call #45: model=ark-code-latest provider=custom in=102671 out=648 total=103319 ``` ## Root Cause Analysis (optional) - The placeholder matches the fallback predicate in `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/tool/fallback-model` (`part.result === undefined && part.completedAt !== undefined` → unavailable title) — the same predicate as #134342, but here it is not a transient flash: a human-input tool may legitimately wait up to 3600 s. - The unmount happened live (no restart/replay involved). Which path cleared the card — re-arm on session re-entry, a spurious settle, or the blocking-prompt store losing the request — could not be pinned: the packaged renderer has no CDP port, while the gateway verifiably kept the request pending the whole time (no result row, lease held, `tool clarify completed (1278.99s)`). ## Deduplication Searched clarify / "Result unavailable" / blocking-prompt issues; nearest neighbors read and excluded: - #133770 — same component, **inverse** shape (batch card mounted twice, survives restart); here a single-question card mounts zero times after re-entry. The re-arm logic discussed there is the likely shared area. - #134342 — transient "Result unavailable" flash on the live event path; here it is the steady state of a parked human-input call. - #133372 / #137561 / #135339 — clarify strands / lost answers via owner routing, expired locks, typed-reply races; in all of them the answer path is exercised. Here the card was never answerable at all. - #116195 / #113035 / #118481 (closed) — "Result unavailable" where a result exists or the call was interrupted; here no result existed yet. ## Proposed Fix (optional) Direction only: (a) a pending human-input tool call should stay in waiting state — not receive `completedAt` / the unavailable treatment — until an authoritative terminal condition (answer, skip, timeout, interrupt); (b) the card re-arm path should also cover switch-away-and-back for single-question clarifies. --- Companion report: #139190 (same observation window — the "1 Queued" entry visible in the screenshot is the subject of that display-leak report).

### Bug Description

I am experiencing two issues when configuring and using SenseNova with Hermes Agent on Windows.

**Issue 1: Follow-up messages fail**

The first message in a conversation may receive a response, but a subsequent message in the same conversation can fail with:

`HTTP 400: Request extraction failed`

Starting a fresh session allowed a test message to receive a reply again. This may be related to conversation history, follow-up request formatting, or provider compatibility.

**Issue 2: Custom Provider connection rejects the API key after saving**

When I enter my SenseNova API key in the Custom Provider configuration and test the connection, Hermes reports that it found four models.

However, after saving the connection and testing it again, the endpoint rejects the API key and Hermes reports an authentication error.

This is inconsistent with the initial connection test, which successfully discovers four models. The key, provider configuration, environment-variable handling, or differences between the initial test and saved-connection test may be involved, but the root cause has not been established.

Both issues need investigation. They may be related to provider configuration or may be separate bugs.

body:
### Describe the bug

With the A2A platform adapter bound to a non-loopback address (`0.0.0.0`) and **no `A2A_TRUSTED_PEERS` configured**, the adapter rejects **every** inbound peer with `403`:

```
{"code": -32052, "message": "peer 'ip:100.x.y.z' not trusted"}
```

This includes requests coming from the host's own addresses. Failing closed is the right security default, but there is **no startup warning**: the only trace is a single `WARNING` line in `gateway.log`, so after an upgrade the A2A door is silently shut until someone happens to read logs. In our case peer-node inbound traffic had been blocked for several days before it was noticed, and the sending nodes had simply stopped retrying.

### Diagnosis notes (may help others)

* Peer identity is derived as `ip:<client_ip>` (in the A2A adapter's security module), so user/allow-list style config (`A2A_ALLOW_ALL_USERS`) cannot help — the trust list needs `ip:`-prefixed entries.
* Fix that worked: set `A2A_TRUSTED_PEERS=ip:<peer-lan>,ip:<peer-tailnet>,ip:127.0.0.1` and restart the gateway. Verified afterwards: `POST http://127.0.0.1:9900/` → `200 TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`, while a non-listed tailnet IP still returns `403`.
* Adding `ip:127.0.0.1` turned an unverifiable setting into a self-testable one — worth documenting as the recommended way to smoke-test A2A locally.

### To reproduce

1. Enable the A2A platform with `A2A_BEARER_TOKEN` set and bind address `0.0.0.0`.
2. Leave `A2A_TRUSTED_PEERS` unset.
3. Send any JSON-RPC request to `http://<host-lan-or-tailnet-ip>:9900/` carrying the valid bearer token.
4. Observe `403 {"code": -32052, "message": "peer 'ip:…' not trusted"}` — also when calling the host's own address.

### Expected behavior

* At minimum: a loud startup **warning** (or refuse to start) whenever the adapter binds a non-loopback interface and the effective trust list is empty — so "the door is closed" is discoverable without reading logs.
* Ideally also: (a) document the exact env var and the `ip:` prefix requirement in the A2A setup docs, (b) default-allow loopback (and optionally the host's own addresses) so a fresh install always keeps a local self-test path.

### Environment

* Hermes v0.22.0 (adapter fails closed as of the build installed 2026-10-10; last successful inbound before that date)
* A2A adapter: bind `0.0.0.0:9900`, bearer token set, `A2A_TRUSTED_PEERS` unset
* Linux (Arch family), Python 3.14

body:
## Summary

On a **source (git) install**, `hermes update --check` fails with

```
→ Update channel: stable
✗ Could not resolve the stable source channel: api.github.com did not answer within 10 seconds.
```

while, in the same minute, plain `curl` to the **same** endpoint succeeds in under a second and `git fetch --tags` exits 0.

Root cause: `hermes_cli/source_check.py:_request_with()` hard-codes `timeout=10` on a bare `urllib.request.urlopen()`. On Windows, `urllib` discovers the system proxy from the registry, so the request *does* go through the proxy — but a **cold TLS handshake through that proxy routinely costs more than 10 s**, so the very first request of a session times out. The PATH/network is fine; the ceiling is too tight. There is no retry and no env/config override for this value.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro, git (source) install of `NousResearch/hermes-agent`
- Version: **v0.22.2** — `Hermes Agent v0.22.2 (2026.9.24) · stable · local d923a5eb487a` (commit `d923a5eb487a17c0a68801bba9ef0f56c81040a8`)
- Network: mainland China. Direct TLS to `api.github.com` is reachable for small requests; a local Clash Verge proxy is running on `127.0.0.1:7897` and is registered as the **Windows system proxy**
- `urllib.request.getproxies()` in the Hermes venv returns:
  `{'http': 'http://127.0.0.1:7897', 'https': 'http://127.0.0.1:7897', 'ftp': 'http://127.0.0.1:7897'}`
  → the proxy **is** picked up, this is not a "proxy ignored" case

## Reproduction

```bash
# fails (exit 1)
hermes update --check
#  → Update channel: stable
#  ✗ Could not resolve the stable source channel: api.github.com did not answer within 10 seconds.

# same endpoint, same minute, plain curl
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}\n' https://api.github.com/repos/NousResearch/hermes-agent/releases/latest
#  → 200 0.66

# and the git path is healthy too
git -C <install>/hermes-agent fetch origin main --tags
#  → rc=0 (fetched tags v0.22.0 / v0.22.1 / v0.22.2)
```

## Measured evidence (same host, same endpoint, Hermes venv python)

Exact call shape the updater uses (`urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10)`, UA `hermes-update-check`):

| # | timeout used | result | elapsed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (cold, first request of the session) | 10 s | **FAIL** `URLError: <urlopen error _ssl.c:999: The handshake operation timed out>` | 10.2 s |
| 2 (immediately after) | 60 s | OK | 3.0 s |
| 3–8 (warm) | 10 s | OK ×6 | 1.0 s, 1.4 s, 1.1 s, 1.0 s, 1.2 s, 1.1 s |

So the ceiling is hit only on the **cold** connection, and once the connection is warm the same 10 s is ample. Anything between roughly 3 s and 10 s of handshake variance flips the whole check into a false failure.

Same behaviour during an actual upgrade: `hermes update --yes --keep-stash --channel stable` **exited 1 on its first attempt and succeeded on retry** (total 44.7 min). The failure is transient/timeout-shaped, not a broken network — but `hermes update --check` has no equivalent retry, so the user only ever sees the failure.

## Root cause

`hermes_cli/source_check.py` (v0.22.2):

```python
def _request_with(url: str, accept: str, token: str | None) -> str:
    headers = {"Accept": accept, "User-Agent": "hermes-update-check"}
    if token:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=headers)
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as response:      # <- hard-coded 10 s
        return response.read(2 * 1024 * 1024).decode("utf-8-sig").strip()
```

- The only "retry" in `_request()` is the **HTTP 401** token→anonymous fallback; a `TimeoutError` is not retried at all.
- No proxy argument (relies on `urllib`'s implicit discovery) and **no `HERMES_*` / config override** for this timeout — `grep` for env reads in this module yields only `HERMES_REVISION`.
- The user-facing sentence comes from `hermes_cli/github_api.py:97`/`:100`, which maps any `TimeoutError`/`URLError(reason=TimeoutError)` to the literal string `"api.github.com did not answer within 10 seconds."` — a **hard-coded 10** in the message that will silently lie if the value is ever changed.

## Why the message misleads

It names a connectivity failure, so the natural next step is to check the network — but `curl` and `git` both work against the same host in the same minute. The real remedy is "re-run it a second time", which the message never suggests, and which `hermes update --check` cannot do for itself.

## How this differs from the existing reports

- **#114736 / #114814** (closed, desktop) — `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:fetchGitHubApiOnce()` using Node's `https` and ignoring `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`. That was a *proxy not honoured* bug in the **TypeScript/Electron** path. Here the proxy **is** honoured (see `getproxies()` above); the failure is the 10 s ceiling in the **Python CLI** path (`hermes_cli/source_check.py`), which the desktop fix does not touch. `hermes update --check` reproduces it from a plain terminal, with no desktop involved.
- **#90638** (open PR) — raises the hard-coded 10 s on the **git probes** (`_upstream_main_sha()`'s `git ls-remote`, `_check_via_local_git()`'s `git fetch`) to 30 s and makes it configurable. Same problem class, **different call sites**: it does not cover the `api.github.com` HTTPS call in `source_check._request_with()`, which is the one that actually fails here (the `git fetch` probe succeeds).
- **#137244** (open) — the 60 s **git transport** timeout being misreported as "No published stable release could be verified". Different probe, different message.
- **#124022** (open) — "updater sets no proxy": about env/config proxy plumbing. Our case has a working proxy and still fails; if a proxy fix lands, the 10 s ceiling would remain a latent flake.

## Suggested fix

1. Raise the ceiling and/or make it configurable, consistent with what #90638 does for the git probes, e.g. `HERMES_UPDATE_HTTP_TIMEOUT` (default 30 s) read in `source_check._request_with()`.
2. Retry the request **once** on `TimeoutError` (the existing 401 fallback already shows the shape of such a retry) — the measurements above show a single retry converts every observed failure into a success.
3. Stop hard-coding `10` inside the user-facing message in `github_api.py`; derive it from the actual timeout so the message cannot drift.

## Workaround for users on the same network

Re-run `hermes update --check` a second time — the first call warms the proxy connection and subsequent calls complete in ~1 s. `hermes update` itself already recovers via its built-in retry.

body:
### Bug Description

On the gateway-owned ACP path, `session/set_model` ignores the `provider:` prefix of the model id. The ids are the ones Hermes itself advertises (an ACP client such as Paseo lists `deepseek:deepseek-flash`, `anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5`, … from Hermes' own `session/new` response). Picking a model of a *different provider* than the session's current one therefore does not switch provider:

- **Switching inside a running chat:** the whole string is read as a model name of the current provider and normalised to `vendor/model`. A chat on `provider=anthropic` switched to `deepseek:deepseek-flash` sends `model=deepseek/deepseek-flash` to `https://api.anthropic.com`, which answers 404 on every turn.
- **Choosing the model when the chat is created (default profile only):** in my control test the requested cross-provider model was not used and the chat ran on the profile's default model (details below). I did not trace why creation behaves that way; I only observed the outcome. I could not make this work on a profile whose own provider is a `process://` plugin, with or without the patch (see below).

The legacy ACP path (`acp_adapter/server.py::_switch_model`) does `explicit_provider, model_input = parse_model_input(raw_model, "")` first ("`provider:model` picker ids become `--provider`"). The gateway path (`acp_adapter/gateway_server.py::set_session_model`) builds `payload = {'model': model_id}` with no provider, and `gateway/session_mutation_model.py::prepare_model` passes `raw_input=payload['model']`, `explicit_provider=payload.get('provider', '')` to `switch_model`. Nothing in between splits the prefix. The same function on current `main` (73b9f2af7b, 2026-10-15) is unchanged, so the bug is still there (I compared the file, I did not run `main`).

A second, smaller problem: the failure is reported as "<Provider> didn't answer after 3 attempts — it looks temporarily unavailable. Wait a minute and send /retry". It is an HTTP 404 `not_found_error` for the model name, which cannot be fixed by waiting, and it is retried 3 times first.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. ACP client on the gateway path, a session running `provider=anthropic model=claude-sonnet-5-5`.
2. Send `session/set_model` with `modelId: "deepseek:deepseek-flash"` (a configured provider with a valid key).
3. Send any prompt.

(I used Paseo 0.11.1; its model picker sends exactly that id.)

### Expected Behavior

`deepseek:deepseek-flash` switches the session to provider `deepseek`, model `deepseek-flash` (what the legacy path and `/model deepseek:deepseek-flash` do).

### Actual Behavior

```
agent.turn_context: conversation turn: session=… model=deepseek/deepseek-flash provider=anthropic …
ERROR agent.chat_completion_helpers: Streaming failed before delivery: Error code: 404 - {'type': 'error', 'error': {'type': 'not_found_error', 'message': 'model: deepseek/deepseek-flash'}, …}
WARNING agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=NotFoundError provider=anthropic base_url=https://api.anthropic.com model=deepseek/deepseek-flash summary=HTTP 404: model: deepseek/deepseek-flash
```

Same with `openrouter:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` (turn ran as `model=openrouter:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash provider=anthropic`).

Controlled test on a profile with `model.provider: deepseek`, `model.default: deepseek-flash` (values are the `model=… provider=…` of `agent.turn_context` in `agent.log`):

- **Unpatched:** a throwaway chat created with model `anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5`, then `set_model deepseek:deepseek-flash`, each followed by a prompt. Both prompts were answered, but the log contains **no** `claude-haiku-5-5` / `anthropic` turn; every turn logged is `deepseek-flash` / `deepseek` (the profile default). I.e. the cross-provider model I asked for was never used. (The log showed two sessions with one turn each rather than the three turns I expected, so I can't say more than that no haiku turn happened.)
- **Patched (diff below), same script:** turn 1 `claude-haiku-5-5` / `anthropic`, then after `set_model deepseek:deepseek-flash` turn 2 `deepseek-flash` / `deepseek`. A second script, created on `deepseek:deepseek-flash` → `set_model anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5` → `set_model deepseek:deepseek-flash`, logged `deepseek-flash/deepseek` → `claude-haiku-5-5/anthropic` → `deepseek-flash/deepseek`.

On a second profile whose default is `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` / `claude-opus-5-5[1m]` (a `process://` provider), chats created with `--model deepseek:deepseek-flash` also ran `claude-opus-5-5[1m]` — **but they still do after the patch below, so that case is NOT explained by this bug** and I have not found its cause. Part of #134889, the post-merge fixes for the unified gateway (#106742). This package collects 10 open findings in one area, so one person working with sub-agents can take all of them. ## Direction: follow #106742

body:
Part of #134889, the post-merge fixes for the unified gateway (#106742). This package collects 16 open findings in one area, so one person working with sub-agents can take all of them. The area is the classic CLI (`hermes chat`) as a client of the shared gateway. That covers switching and resuming sessions, command output, worktrees, `/queue`, and work that still runs in the CLI process.

Sibling packages: #139160 (package 2, session creation, model picks and credentials) · #139161 (package 3, Ink TUI and Desktop) · #139162 (package 4, bots, cron and Kanban). Shared files are named in the lane notes; check with that package's assignee before changing them.

## Direction: follow #106742

Every fix in this package must honor the vision and direction of the one-gateway PR, [#106742](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/106742) (`feat/unified-gateway-runtime`, merged to `main` on Oct 14). Read its description before starting, and put this section in the brief of every sub-agent you spawn.

- One gateway owns every local session: one FIFO, one durable queue, one writer. Fix the gateway path. Don't bring back a client-side agent, a local fallback, or a second writer to `state.db`.
- Clients only read and submit. A missing capability gets a gateway handler or a named refusal, not client-side state.
- Keep the contract: queued admissions survive an owner restart and run FIFO exactly once; a started admission that loses its owner becomes interrupted and is never replayed automatically; a retry reuses the original admission identity and payload.
- Profile, provider, generation and revision boundaries hold on every transport.
- If a fix seems to need a step away from this design, stop and ask on #134889 before writing it.

## Working rules

- Branch from current `main`. 🟡 rows haven't been reproduced: reproduce on `main` first. If one doesn't reproduce, say so on #134889 instead of fixing it.
- Lanes touch different code, so they can run in parallel in separate worktrees. Open one PR per lane (split a lane if it grows), each with a failing test first.
- Name the row ID in each PR (`Refs #134889 (CLI-11)`) and reference this issue. `Fixes` is fine for a row's own bug report (e.g. `Fixes #138843`), never for #134889.
- **An open PR from an outside contributor doesn't cover a row.** Review it. If it's right, finish it: push small fixes to the contributor's branch when it allows maintainer edits, or salvage it into your PR with `Co-authored-by` credit. If it's wrong or stale, fix the row fresh and say why on that PR.
- Steps, evidence and code locations are in the source comments linked under each section of the tracker's [open findings](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#open-findings).

## Findings

Status: 🔴 confirmed live · 🟡 static read or user report, not reproduced yet

### Lane 1: Switching and resuming sessions

title: Gateway fixes (#134889), package 1: classic CLI

body:
### Problem or Use Case

I want this Telegram reply behaviour:

- Replies are text by default, including when I send a voice note.
- If I explicitly ask for audio ("reply in voice", or `/voice audio`), replies in that session become one voice note each, with no text: no streamed text, no caption, no follow-up text bubble.
- That mode stays on for later turns until I explicitly ask for text again.
- A new session (`/new`, a new thread, or an idle reset) starts in text again. Other chats and platforms are unaffected.

Core `/voice` can't express this:

1. **Scope.** `GatewayRunner._voice_mode` is keyed per chat (`_voice_key_for_source`) and persisted to `gateway_voice_mode.json`, so a mode survives across sessions indefinitely. There's no way to scope it to one session or thread.
2. **Modality.** `voice_only` and `all` always deliver the text too. The runner path (`_send_voice_reply`, used when streaming consumed the response) sends text plus audio. The adapter auto-TTS path (`BasePlatformAdapter._play_tts_file`) attaches the text as the Telegram caption.
3. **Trigger.** `voice_only` keys on the input modality (voice in → voice out). Here the trigger is an explicit request and is independent of the input: text-in turns get audio while the mode is on, and voice-in turns get text while it's off.

Today I get this behaviour from a plugin that wraps four private seams at runtime: `GatewayRunner._hmwa_deliver_turn_response`, `GatewayRunner._should_send_voice_reply`, `TurnRunner._setup_stream_consumer` (to suppress streaming for the turn) and `BasePlatformAdapter._should_auto_tts_for_chat`. It works, but any refactor of those signatures breaks it, so I run a signature check after every `hermes update`.

### Proposed Solution

Add a session-scoped reply modality next to the existing per-chat voice mode:

- **State.** `reply_modality: "text" | "audio"`, stored on the session (e.g. a field on the `SessionEntry`/session store, or `session_key`-keyed in the runner), **not** in `gateway_voice_mode.json`. A new session starts at `text` (or at a configurable default). Session continuations such as compression children inherit the parent's value.
- **Precedence.** When the session value is set, it overrides the per-chat `/voice` mode and `voice.auto_tts` for that session. When it's unset, behaviour is unchanged.
- **`audio` delivery.**
  - Turn streaming is disabled for the turn (same mechanism as `voice.suppress_text` in #99632).
  - The final response goes through TTS and is sent as a voice message with **no caption** and **no separate text** (same delivery as `gateway.tts_reply_text: false` in #114045).
  - Fail-open: if synthesis or the voice send fails, the text is delivered as a normal message, the failure is logged, and the mode stays `audio` for the next turn.
  - Dedup: if the agent already called `text_to_speech` this turn, don't synthesize a second voice note (the existing check in `_should_send_voice_reply`).
- **`text` delivery.** No auto-TTS for the session, even for voice-in turns and even when the per-chat mode or `voice.auto_tts` would speak.
- **Switching.**
  - A command, e.g. `/voice audio` and `/voice text`, or `/reply audio|text`. Sessions are the scope by default; the existing `/voice on|off|tts` keep their per-chat meaning.
  - A public API for plugins, e.g. `runner.set_session_reply_modality(session_key, "audio" | "text" | None)` plus a getter. This would let a `pre_gateway_dispatch` hook map natural-language requests ("responde em áudio", "back to text") to the mode without core doing intent detection.
  - Optionally, the switch could be exposed as an agent tool so the model can act on an explicit request itself. A plugin hook covers this, so it isn't required.

With this in place, the plugin would keep only its intent detection and call the public setter. The four runtime wrappers could go.

### Alternatives Considered

- **#99619 / PR #99632 (`voice.suppress_text`)** and **#137892 / PR #114045 (`gateway.tts_reply_text`)** solve the duplicate-text half (point 2), and either is a good building block. Both are global config gated on *voice input*, though, so neither covers per-session scope or an explicit switch that's independent of the input modality (points 1 and 3). If one of them lands, this issue becomes "add session scope + switch API on top of it".
- **#132451 / PR #132441** (adapter-declared spoken replies) is per platform, not per session.
- **Keep the plugin.** It works today but depends on four private methods. A public setter and a session-level field would remove that fragility.
- **Per-chat `/voice` with a hook that resets it on `/new`.** This still delivers text alongside audio, and resetting persisted per-chat state from a session hook is racy across threads in the same chat.

### Feature Type

Gateway / messaging improvement

### Scope

Medium (a few files): session state + precedence in `run_voice.py`, streaming suppression for the turn, adapter delivery flag, command handling in `slash_commands.py`, and tests.

### Contribution

- [ ] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

I can run the plugin's behavioural scenarios against a core implementation: default voice-in → text, request audio → audio only, sticky across turns, switch back to text, new session resets, compression child inherits, other platforms untouched, TTS failure → text fallback, and no duplicate when the agent already called `text_to_speech`.

**Version:** Hermes Agent v0.22.1+66.g7bda2a3 (PM-managed, Python 3.14.7, linux-arm64). The code below is unchanged on `origin/main` 73b9f2af7b (2026-10-15).

**What happens**

A Kanban task assigned to a profile whose model goes through an `anthropic_messages` endpoint that is not Anthropic never reaches the model. Profile config:

```yaml
model:
  default: MiniMax-M2.7
  provider: custom:minimax          # also with provider: minimax + base_url
  base_url: https://api.minimax.io/anthropic
  api_mode: anthropic_messages
custom_providers:
  - name: minimax
    base_url: https://api.minimax.io/anthropic
    key_env: MINIMAX_API_KEY        # set in the profile's .env; with or without api_key: ''
    api_mode: anthropic_messages
```

`hermes -p <profile> chat -q "…"` works. The same profile as a Kanban worker fails on every call:

```
agent.stream_diag: Stream drop on attempt 1/3 — retrying. provider=custom:minimax base_url=https://api.minimax.io/anthropic
  error_type=APIConnectionError error=Connection error.
  chain=APIConnectionError(Connection error.) <- LocalProtocolError(Illegal header value b'Bearer ')
agent.conversation_loop: Provider unavailable (timeout) — auto-recovery cycle 5/5, retrying in 60s
```

The task stays `running` for ~10 minutes of retries, with `api_call_count` 0. A profile on `provider: anthropic` (Kody here) runs the same task in seconds.

**Why**

1. `gateway/session_kanban.py` builds the worker policy without an API key, so `launch_key()` returns `None` and `agent/managed_worker.py` constructs `AIAgent(..., api_key=None)`. (Interactive gateway sessions resolve the key before construction.)
2. In `agent/agent_init.py`, the `anthropic_messages` branch does not resolve a missing key for non-native providers:

   ```python
   # _init_anthropic_client, line 761
   _is_native_anthropic = agent.provider == "anthropic"
   effective_key = api_key or (resolve_anthropic_token(...) if _is_native_anthropic else None) or ""
   ```

   so `effective_key == ""`, and the SDK sends `Authorization: Bearer ` (MiniMax uses Bearer auth). The OpenAI-wire branch does not have this gap: `_init_openai_client` falls back to `_routed_client_kwargs()` when `api_key` or `base_url` is missing.

Minimal reproduction, in the profile's environment with its `.env` loaded:

```python
AIAgent(model="MiniMax-M2.7", provider="custom:minimax", base_url="https://api.minimax.io/anthropic", api_key=None).api_key  # -> ""
AIAgent(model="MiniMax-M2.7", provider="minimax", base_url="https://api.minimax.io/anthropic", api_key=None).api_key        # -> ""
AIAgent(model="MiniMax-M2.7", provider="minimax", base_url=None, api_key=None).api_key                                        # -> the key (routed, chat_completions)
```

**Suggested fix** (either):

- `_init_anthropic_client`: when `api_key` is empty and the provider is not native Anthropic, resolve that provider's own credential (the same resolution `resolve_runtime_provider()` does for the CLI: `custom_providers[].api_key` / `key_env`, the provider's env vars, the credential pool) before falling back to `""`; or
- `build_kanban_policy()`: resolve and bind the launch key for the worker as interactive sessions do.

Also worth failing fast: an empty key currently surfaces as a transient `APIConnectionError` and goes through every auto-recovery cycle. A "no API key for provider X" error at construction would have pointed straight at the cause.

**Workaround:** use the built-in `provider: minimax` with no `base_url` / `api_mode` in the model section; the routed OpenAI-wire path resolves `MINIMAX_API_KEY`.

body:
## Bug Description

After `hermes update` to v0.22.0 (0.21.6 → 0.22.0) the CLI can no longer start: `hermes`, `hermes --cli` and `hermes chat` all print a few blank lines followed by a bare `Error: invalid_params` and exit 1. `hermes --version` works, so the install itself is intact.

Root cause: the classic CLI now creates its session through the gateway (`hermes_cli/gateway_session_store.py`, new in v0.22.0, commit `9748e38caa1` "feat(cli): HermesCLI's agent and session store are the gateway's") and sends the config-resolved `toolsets` list verbatim in `session.create`. The gateway validates every name with `toolsets.validate_toolset()` in `gateway/session_policy.py::_resolve_toolsets`, which only accepts registry-resident toolsets. An MCP server's toolset alias is registered **only after a successful connect** (`tools/mcp_tool_registration.py` → `registry.register_toolset_alias(name, f"mcp-{name}")), so a **configured but currently unreachable** MCP server makes the whole launch fail.

The CLI's own validator already tolerates exactly this — `hermes_cli/cli_init_mixin.py::_init_toolsets` says "MCP server names only resolve after discover_mcp_tools runs; skip them here", and `hermes_cli/toolset_validation.py::saved_toolset_resolver` documents it as intended: "neither is registered before MCP discovery; a disabled server is inactive, not a typo". Only the new gateway-side check disagrees, and it turns a missing optional dependency into an unstartable install with no actionable message.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install v0.22.0 (git install) by upgrading from v0.21.6 with `hermes update`.
2. Have an MCP server in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` that cannot complete its first connect. In my case it is a remote Streamable-HTTP server whose origin is down (Cloudflare answers HTTP 522):

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  hermes-docs:
    connect_timeout: 60
    timeout: 30
    url: https://mcp.hermesagent.org.cn/v1
```

3. Run `hermes` (any surface — default, `--cli`, `chat`).

## Expected Behavior

`hermes` starts; the unreachable MCP server is simply inactive for that session (its tools absent), exactly as in v0.21.6.

## Actual Behavior

```
$ hermes
Error: invalid_params
$ echo $?
1
```

The gateway's raw error frame (note: **no `fields` key**, so it is raised inside the handler at `gateway/session_controls.py:197`, not by the contract check at line 170):

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"error":{"code":4001,"message":"invalid_params","data":{"reason":"invalid_params"}}}
```

The client's `session.create` params were: `request_id`, `source`, `cwd`, `row_cwd`, `toolsets` — 18 alphabetically sorted names coming from `_get_platform_tools(CLI_CONFIG, "cli")` (`cli.py:1514`, the `not toolsets` branch). Of those 18 names, the only one `validate_toolset()` rejects is the unreachable MCP server's.

## Environment

- Hermes: v0.22.0+2207.g5e90837 (upstream `5e908370`), git install, updated from v0.21.6+302.g73162b0
- OS: Linux x86_64, Python 3.14.7
- The MCP server entry predates the update (v0.21.6 started fine with the identical config), so the config change is not what broke it.

## Root Cause Analysis

Two validators disagree about the same name on the two sides of one RPC:

| side | code | set it accepts |
|---|---|---|
| client | `cli.py:1514` → `_get_platform_tools(CLI_CONFIG, "cli")` | config-derived; includes `mcp_servers` keys via `_merge_mcp_servers`, never requires a live registration |
| gateway | `gateway/session_policy.py::_resolve_toolsets` | `toolsets.validate_toolset(name)` = static `TOOLSETS` ∪ plugin registry ∪ registry **aliases** — aliases exist only after a successful MCP connect |

The wire therefore carries a name the receiving side cannot accept, and `session.create` is refused before the session exists. Anything that keeps an MCP server from completing its first connect — outage, DNS, auth, proxy, slow start during a gateway restart — makes `hermes` unstartable.

## Suggested Fix

Give `_resolve_toolsets` the same acceptance set the platform resolver already uses (I patched this locally and verified it; the negative cases still refuse):

```diff
--- a/gateway/session_policy.py
+++ b/gateway/session_policy.py
@@ def _resolve_toolsets(params, config, source, safe_mode):
     """Validate explicit toolsets and return the session's enabled toolset set."""
     from hermes_cli.tools_config import _get_platform_tools
-    from toolsets import validate_toolset
+    from hermes_cli.toolset_validation import saved_toolset_resolver
+    # Same acceptance set as _get_platform_tools below: registered toolsets PLUS the names this
+    # config declares. An MCP server registers its toolset alias only AFTER a live connect, so a
+    # configured-but-unreachable server is inactive, not a typo.
+    is_valid_toolset = saved_toolset_resolver(config)
     explicit = params.get('toolsets')
     if 'toolsets' in params:
-        if (not isinstance(explicit, list) or any(not isinstance(x, str) or not validate_toolset(x) for x in explicit)
+        if (not isinstance(explicit, list) or any(not isinstance(x, str) or not is_valid_toolset(x) for x in explicit)
                 or ('desktop_ui' in explicit and source !='gui')):
             raise RuntimeStoreError('invalid_params')
```

Verified locally: the original failing list (18 names including the unreachable MCP server) now passes, while a genuinely unknown name, a non-string entry and `desktop_ui` on a `cli` source are still refused with `invalid_params`.

A second, independent option worth considering: `_creation_policy` / `_ensure_gateway_session` should send only the **explicitly requested** launch flags. `-t/--toolsets` is documented as "Comma-separated toolsets to enable for this invocation" with default `None`, so the expanded config-derived list arguably should not ride on the wire at all — the gateway can resolve it from its own config, as it already does when `toolsets` is absent.

Workarounds for anyone hitting this today:
- set `mcp_servers.<name>.enabled: false`, or
- launch with an explicit list: `hermes -t web,terminal,skills,...`

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

Yes — happy to open one if the maintainers agree with the direction above.

## What

Make the per-process `watch_patterns` **lifetime delivery budget configurable**, with today's value as the default and the existing protections unchanged.

Suggested shape (either is fine):

```yaml
# config.yaml
processes:
  watch_lifetime_max_hits: 8      # default: 8 (today's behaviour)
```
or an env override read next to the other bounded-terminal knobs, e.g. `HERMES_WATCH_LIFETIME_MAX_HITS`.
Optionally an explicit opt-in (`watch_lifetime_max_hits: unbounded`) for operators who accept the cost, still gated by the 15 s cooldown and the 3-strike breaker.

## Why

Supervised, long-lived background legs (CI watchers, deploy monitors, agent-orchestration mailboxes) legitimately emit **more than 8 marker lines over their lifetime**. Today the 8th delivery silently promotes the process to `notify_on_complete`, so the operator **stops receiving exactly the signals the patterns were configured for**, with no error and no way to opt out — the only trace is a single `watch_disabled` summary that is easy to miss on a busy session.

Real case: a coordinator agent ran a mailbox watcher leg and a run-status watcher leg; each announced a handful of real events (task settle, delivery, needs-action) and then went quiet after the cap, so the agent sat idle while work completed. Diagnosis took a while precisely because the demotion is quiet.

## Evidence (v0.22.1-66-g7bda2a33680)

`tools/process_registry.py`:

```python
WATCH_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 15
WATCH_STRIKE_LIMIT = 3
WATCH_LIFETIME_MAX_HITS = 8          # ← hard-coded, no config/env override anywhere
...
lifetime_exhausted = session._watch_hits >= WATCH_LIFETIME_MAX_HITS
if lifetime_exhausted:
    session._watch_disabled = True
    session.notify_on_complete = True
```

I searched the whole tree: those three constants are assigned in exactly one place, there is no `config.yaml` / schema key for them, and the bundled docs/skill references only document `notify_on_complete`. (Note the file *does* read env for other limits, e.g. `TERMINAL_LOCAL_MEMORY_MAX_MB`, so the pattern exists.)

## Relationship to #93513 (why I am not asking you to just raise the number)

#93513 (closed) is the reason the cap exists: **each match re-injects a message and forces a full-context agent turn**, which stalls the event loop on large sessions. So this request deliberately keeps:

* the default at **8** (no behaviour change for anyone),
* the **15 s** minimum spacing,
* the **3 consecutive-strike** breaker,
* `notify_on_complete` promotion on exhaustion.

It only adds a **documented, bounded opt-in** for operators whose legs are genuinely long-lived, and makes the exhaustion **visible in config/docs** rather than only discoverable by reading the source.

## Workaround today (not a blocker)

Watch is still needed for rare one-shots, so I re-mount legs that exit at the budget (`notify_on_complete` is not subject to this cap) and re-arm from that exit notification. That works, but it means every operator rebuilds the same machinery.

## Environment

* Hermes `v0.22.1-66-g7bda2a33680` (macOS 27.0.1, local install)
* Background legs via `terminal(background=true, notify=[...], persist_on_release=true)`

## Related

* #93513 — why the cap exists (each match forces a full-context turn)
* #75065 — silent-outcome failures around watch notification delivery
* #29177 — `session_reset.bg_process_max_age_hours` (the adjacent knob that *is* configurable)

### Bug Description

When the network path to the IRC server dies without closing the TCP connection (a NAT or router forgetting the flow, a Wi-Fi or VPN switch, laptop sleep), the IRC adapter never notices. The bot never reconnects, and every DM and channel message is lost until the gateway is restarted by hand. `gateway status` keeps reporting IRC as connected.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the gateway with IRC pointed at a server (seen with Ergo 2.19.1 in Docker) through a TCP relay, and DM the bot from another IRC user. It replies.
2. Make the relay drop the bot's open connection in both directions without closing either side, the way an evicted NAT mapping behaves. New connections still pass.
3. The server times the bot out (`Ping timeout: 2m30s`). Keep DMing the bot.

### Expected Behavior

The adapter notices the dead connection and the gateway reconnects it, as it already does when the server closes the socket.

### Actual Behavior

The bot never comes back. None of the 16 DMs sent over the next 16 minutes was answered; from the server's timeout on, each got `401 No such nick`. The gateway logged nothing for IRC.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

IRC

### Operating System

Windows 11 (gateway from source), Ergo in Docker

### Python Version

3.14

### Hermes Version

main (ecac27c0af, 2026-10-15)

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`_receive_loop` in `plugins/platforms/irc/adapter.py` waits on `self._reader.read(4096)` with no timeout, and the adapter only answers the server's `PING`s. The `connection_lost` fatal error (which the gateway's reconnect watcher picks up) fires only on EOF or a socket error, and a silently dropped path delivers neither. The bot only writes when replying, so nothing provokes a reset either.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Time out the read: after two minutes of silence send `PING`; after four, leave the loop so the existing `connection_lost` path reconnects. Servers PING idle clients every minute or two (Ergo: 90 s), so a healthy link never gets near the window.

### Bug Description

Since the durable native re-authorization step (cc0cd5c993, "recheck native Discord membership before durable admission and claim"), a Discord profile whose `allowed_roles` is configured under `platforms.discord` drops **every** message from role-authorized users with `permission_denied`.

Ingress and re-authorization resolve the role allowlist from different config locations:

- Ingress — `plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py` `_get_allowed_roles()` → `_gate_raw("allowed_roles", "DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES")`: scoped env / snapshot, else `config.extra["allowed_roles"]`. `PlatformConfig.from_dict` (`gateway/config.py` ~L448-452, #10206) fills `extra` from the flat `platforms.discord.allowed_roles` spelling and from `platforms.discord.extra.allowed_roles`. So the user is admitted and `role_authorized=True`.
- Re-authorization — `plugins/platforms/discord/adapter_authorization.py` L12-18, `reauthorize_native_roles.policy()`: only scoped env `DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES` or top-level `read_raw_config()["discord"]["allowed_roles"]`. `platforms.discord.allowed_roles` / `.extra.allowed_roles` are never read, so `roles` is empty → `return False`.

`gateway/session_ingress_context.py` `reauthorize_roles` then raises `RuntimeStoreError('permission_denied')` and the message is dropped silently from the user's point of view.

This is the same class #72348 / #72427 settled for ingress ("read gate config from per-adapter extra, not process-global env"): the new re-authorization path does not follow that rule.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a (multiplexed) profile with roles only under `platforms:`:
   ```yaml
   platforms:
     discord:
       enabled: true
       allowed_roles:
         - '<role id>'
   ```
   (no top-level `discord.allowed_roles`, no `DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES` in the profile `.env`)
2. From a guild member who is authorized only through that role (not in `allow_from`), mention the bot.
3. The message is admitted at ingress, then dropped.

A self-contained regression test against a real temp `HERMES_HOME` is in the linked PR; it fails on current main (`3bdb82d6ec`).

### Expected Behavior

Re-authorization reads the same role policy as ingress, re-read from current config so revocation still works, and the role-authorized user's message is processed. "Same policy" means the scoped env first, then the Discord `extra` exactly as `load_gateway_config()` resolves it. In that resolution `platforms.discord.extra` wins over the top-level `discord:` block (`config_loader._authored_wins`), and `gateway.platforms.discord` and `discord.extra` are accepted too.

When roles are set in more than one place, re-authorization currently disagrees with ingress in both directions. Multiplex mode, real loader:

| config | ingress roles | re-auth grants |
|---|---|---|
| `discord:[3]` + `platforms.discord.extra:[2]` | `[2]` | role 3 only |
| `discord:[]` + `platforms.discord.extra:[2]` | `[2]` | nobody |
| `discord:[3]` + `platforms.discord.extra:[]` | `[]` | role 3 (revocation in `extra` not honoured) |
| `gateway.platforms.discord.allowed_roles:[2]` | `[2]` | nobody |
| `discord.extra.allowed_roles:[2]` | `[2]` | nobody |

### Actual Behavior

```
ERROR gateway.platforms.base: [Discord] Error handling message: permission_denied
  File "gateway/session_envelope.py", line 117, in prepare_native
    fresh_roles = await reauthorize_roles(runner, frozen.source, provenance)
  File "gateway/session_ingress_context.py", line 211, in reauthorize_roles
    raise RuntimeStoreError('permission_denied')
hermes_state_runtime.RuntimeStoreError: permission_denied
```

In our deployment, after upgrading to v0.22.1, 2 of 2 inbound messages on the affected profile failed this way. A profile that also had top-level `discord.allowed_roles` (same role ID) was unaffected.

**Workaround:** duplicate the role IDs into top-level `discord.allowed_roles` in each affected profile's `config.yaml`. `read_raw_config` is cached on file signature, so no restart is needed.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Discord)

### Debug Report

Not attached: this is a company deployment and `hermes debug share` would publish its config and logs to a public paste. The redacted traceback above and the regression test in the PR cover the failure path; happy to provide more specific excerpts on request.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.22.1 (2026.9.24), upstream 297552a9, Docker install
- Python 3.14.7
- Also present on current main `3bdb82d6ec` (`adapter_authorization.py` unchanged)

cc @teknium1 (author of cc0cd5c993)

## Problem

A standalone security/grounding plugin cannot currently rely on one documented public boundary that runs before every externally visible model-derived byte. Individual post-response hooks are insufficient when output may leave through streams, progress, background work, TTS/media, retries, errors, attachments, or proxy delivery.

## Proposed public contract

Add a versioned, capability-gated pre-egress enforcement API owned by the host. It should receive trusted destination/principal/session metadata, output type, correlation IDs, policy revision, and a bounded candidate payload, and return an allow/block/redact decision before emission.

The contract must cover all supported sinks consistently and define ordering relative to streaming, retries, delivery receipts, and revocation.

## Required semantics

- zero model-derived bytes are emitted before an allow decision
- timeout, crash, missing context, or unknown output type fails closed
- retries and alternate sinks cannot bypass the same decision
- revocation/policy revision is checked at emission time
- structured media/attachments are represented without forcing raw secret-bearing blobs into logs
- decisions are auditable with bounded, redacted metadata

## Acceptance tests

A synthetic sink matrix should cover local/proxy responses, token streams, progress, background completion, TTS/media, errors, retries, and attachments, proving block/redact behavior before any observable emission.

This complements broader lifecycle proposals such as #100655; it requests a stable generic plugin enforcement surface rather than application-specific Core changes.

## Problem

A standalone policy plugin can observe some lifecycle/tool hooks, but it lacks one documented host-owned contract that binds an immutable authorization decision to a turn, its tool surface, memory/session isolation, and later revocation. Reconstructing this with private imports or monkey patches is unsafe and unsupported.

## Proposed public contract

Expose a versioned, capability-gated API that lets the host provide a read-only turn authorization context containing trusted principal/channel/session scope, policy revision, permitted tool identifiers, memory/profile isolation mode, and a revocation token/fence.

The host—not plugin/model arguments—must enforce the resulting tool allow-set at schema exposure and again immediately before execution. An explicitly empty set must remain empty.

## Revocation semantics

A committed revocation should invalidate or cancel stale turns, tool calls, cached agents, session reads, attachment reads, and pending delivery associated with the older policy revision. Failures or unknown state must deny rather than fall back to ambient permissions.

## Acceptance tests

- empty allow-set exposes and executes zero tools
- a stale policy revision cannot execute after revocation commits
- group/session construction cannot inherit private profile memory
- principal/channel scope cannot be supplied by model or plugin input
- cached/retried work is fenced by the same revision
- contract works under supported plugin isolation or reports an explicit unsupported mode

This is a generic public extension request. It must not require host-file edits, private imports, registry mutation, or monkey patching.

## Problem

Standalone plugins cannot safely implement passive group archiving or policy observation from the currently documented general-plugin hooks. A plugin needs a supported event that does not invoke the model and does not require imports from Gateway/platform internals.

## Proposed public contract

Add a versioned, capability-gated plugin subscription for authorized group events. Each event should carry host-issued, immutable fields for profile, platform, chat/group, message, sender, thread, event/replay identity, and authorization revision.

The host should own normalization, authorization, ordering, bounded backpressure, retry/drop semantics, and redaction. The plugin must not be able to assert or rewrite identity.

## Failure and revocation semantics

- fail closed when trusted identity or authorization context is unavailable
- no model invocation is required to receive an event
- duplicate/replay identity is explicit
- revocation prevents later delivery under an obsolete grant
- plugin failures cannot weaken Gateway handling
- multi-profile delivery is bound to the loading profile

## Acceptance tests

- authorized event arrives once with stable trusted identifiers
- duplicate transport delivery is distinguishable and idempotent
- revoked or cross-profile events are denied
- missing/invalid identity fails closed
- slow/crashed plugin behavior is bounded
- no private Gateway/platform import is required

This requests a generic public plugin contract, not plugin-specific code or a Core workaround. Related group-runtime work such as #97681 may provide reusable identity/replay concepts, but this request is specifically for the standalone plugin surface.

### Summary

Desktop's **Messaging → Discord** form (and the other platform forms) only edits the platform's environment-variable settings: `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`, `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS`, `DISCORD_REPLY_TO_MODE`, `DISCORD_HOME_CHANNEL`/`_NAME`. The slash-command **admin tier** can't be configured from Desktop at all:

- `allow_admin_from` / `user_allowed_commands` (DM scope)
- `group_allow_admin_from` / `group_user_allowed_commands` (group scope)

These can only be set in the platform's config.yaml section. `gateway/config_loader.py` copies them into the platform's `extra` dict, which `gateway/slash_access.py` reads. No environment variable maps to them, so the env-driven Desktop form has nowhere to show them.

### Why it matters

Per `gateway/slash_access.py`, admin gating is opt-in. With no `allow_admin_from`, every allowed user gets the full command set, including `/login`, `/yolo`, and so on. A Desktop-only user who sets up a Discord bot and adds a second allowed user has no in-app way to keep those commands to themselves, and no hint that the setting exists.

### Proposed

Add an **Admins** field to each platform's messaging form, next to the existing allowlist field (`apps/desktop/src/app/messaging/allowlist-field.tsx` looks reusable), that writes `allow_admin_from` into that platform's config.yaml section. Optionally add the group-scope and `user_allowed_commands` lists as advanced fields.

A one-line hint under "Allowed users" would already help ("Everyone listed here can run every command unless admins are set").

### Related

- #111641 covers the same gap in the CLI setup wizard and pairing flow (`--admin`). This issue is the Desktop counterpart.
- #67144 / #64250 are broader Desktop ↔ dashboard parity issues. This is one concrete, small gap.

### Summary

In multi-session DM topic mode (`/topic`), a message sent from the **root DM (General / "All Messages")** is delivered thread-less and pinned to the last bound topic's session by the lobby-recovery rule, while an empty new topic may be created by the client. The user never gets moved into a fresh topic for the new conversation — the reply stays in whatever topic was bound last.

This is a behavior change compared to the earlier versions (tested on v0.21.x, worked as of June–October 2026 through `v0.21.5+4536`): a message written in the root DM started a new session in a **newly created topic immediately** — the bot's response landed inside that new topic (auto-renamed to the generated session title), so the topic was never empty and the conversation context visually moved with the thread.

### Current behavior (v0.22.0)

1. Multi-session topic mode enabled (`/topic on`), `telegram_dm_topic_mode.enabled=1`.
2. User writes a message in the root DM.
3. Telegram may create an empty topic; the gateway delivers the message without `message_thread_id`.
4. Lobby recovery pins the message (and the reply) to the **last bound topic's session** instead of opening a new session in the fresh topic.
5. Result: mixed-context conversations ("resume discussion appearing in the topics thread"), user has to manually create a topic first and write the first message inside it.

Related: #136567 (the same thread-less delivery root cause, from the opposite angle — topics misrouting to the previous topic).

### Desired behavior

Restore (or make configurable) the pre-v0.22 flow: a message written in the root DM of a topic-mode chat starts a new session **in a newly created topic**, with the first exchange and the auto-generated title living inside that topic.

### Suggested implementation

A config flag, enabled explicitly so the current lobby semantics stay the default:

```yaml
gateway:
  platforms:
    telegram:
      extra:
        dm_topic_auto_transfer: true   # root-DM message (no thread_id) → create a named topic (seed message), bind a new session, reply inside it
```

Fallback: if topic creation fails (Threaded Mode off, flood limits, `forums_disabled`), keep today's lobby-recovery behavior.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.22.0 (2026.9.24) · stable, Telegram gateway, poll mode, `rich_messages: true`
- Confirmed on live data 2026-10-15:
  - messages sent inside an existing topic always arrive with `message_thread_id` and bind correctly (`agent:main:telegram:dm:{chat}:{thread}` has its own session, binding row created, auto-rename works);
  - messages sent from root DM arrive with `reply_to_id=None` / no thread and resolve to the last-bound topic's session (`gateway.log`: 4 out of 4 messages of the day resolved to `...:346144`);
  - on v0.21.x the same flow produced a topic session immediately (`Flushing text batch agent:main:telegram:dm:<chat>:<new_thread>` followed by `Renamed DM topic ... -> <session title>`).
title: Feature request: option to restore pre-v0.22 auto topic transfer (root-DM message opens a new session in a freshly created topic)

On installed Hermes Agent v0.22.1 (stable v2026.9.24), git revision `297552a9d646119871391d202509822cd86330df`, a native background `delegate_task` canary in a Discord thread completed successfully, but the parent did not receive its completion turn after ending the active turn. A later human continuation was needed to recover the saved result.

The canary ran one harmless foreground terminal command and returned a marker. It did not launch a background process or change project files. The returned child identity was bound to the exact registered delegation through its parent and kickoff goal before reading its records.

## Retained evidence

The exact delegation's canonical ledger record was observed as:

```text
state = completed
result task status = completed
result exit_reason = completed
result truncated = false
result schema_valid = true
delivery_state = pending
delivery_attempts = 0
delivered_at = NULL
delivery_claim = NULL
```

The bound child transcript contains the expected terminal marker, exit code 0 and a final response. Its session/usage records agree on the requested model/provider and successful inference. A supported coarse child-status query reports no live subagents. The gateway user service is active. The completion remained pending when the parent recovered it; it was not manually marked delivered or dropped.

`delivery_attempts=0` is the stored observation, not proof that no admission was ever attempted: deferred admission can return that counter to zero. The source of the missing admission/wake is not yet established. This is one real observed canary, not a claimed deterministic offline reproduction or a lifetime failure rate.

## Reproduction candidate

1. In a Discord thread, dispatch one native background child with a harmless terminal-marker task.
2. Let main do independent work, then end its turn as the exposed tool instructs.
3. Check whether completion actually schedules a new main turn without a human message.
4. If it does not, correlate the exact delegation and child records; distinguish completed/pending from running, delivered, dropped, lease contention and API-server persist-only behavior.

## Related reports and distinction

- #136315 concerns an already-acknowledged `delivered` event lost at the recursion cap; this observation is still `pending`.
- #130226 concerns intentional persist-only `api_server` sessions; this task originated in Discord.
- #131578 concerns child process notifications re-pinning a route; this child launched no background process, and that mechanism is not established here.
- #82703 concerns claim-before-route attempt consumption; the current observation alone does not establish that cause.

## Expected behavior / acceptance

A successfully completed Discord delegation should either reach its owning main session through the supported completion path, or expose a concrete recoverable admission failure instead of silently requiring a human continuation. Preserve correct chat/profile ownership, busy-session/approval boundaries, at-least-once handling and replay semantics. Include a real adapter/ledger-to-parent-turn regression rather than accepting child completion alone.

## Workaround and limits

A supported joined-return `hermes chat -Q --oneshot` run in the same authorized model/provider/effort lane returned its harmless tool result and exit 0 directly to the caller. This is a bounded receiving-path workaround, not an async-delivery fix or proof about long-running jobs.

No Hermes product source, delivery ledger, leases or gateway service were modified during this investigation. Private chat/session/delegation identifiers, personal data, credentials, raw logs and conversation payloads are omitted. An independently clean latest-main reproduction is not claimed.

## What happened

At one gateway startup, seven platform plugins failed within the same second with the identical error:

```
12:12:19 Failed to load plugin 'discord-platform'  : dictionary changed size during iteration

12:12:19 Failed to load plugin 'google_chat-platform': dictionary changed size during iteration
12:12:19 Failed to load plugin 'irc-platform'       : dictionary changed size during iteration

12:12:19 Failed to load plugin 'mattermost-platform': dictionary changed size during iteration
12:12:19 Failed to load plugin 'ntfy-platform'      : dictionary changed size during iteration
```

Same session also had `telegram-platform: load timed out after 10s (import + register() never returned)`.

## Analysis

Seven identical `dictionary changed size during iteration` failures in the same second point to a concurrency race during bulk plugin registration: something mutates the registry dict while the loader iterates it. The failures are all-or-nothing per boot — subsequent startups loaded the same plugins fine.

The telegram case suggests `import` and `register()` share one 10 s budget; a slow import leaves register almost nothing.

## Suggested improvements

- Iterate over a snapshot (`list(registry.items())`) or hold a lock around registry mutation during registration.
- Consider separate budgets for import vs `register()`.

## Environment

- v0.22.1+73.g4278fec, Windows 11

## What happened

While the install had a pending source-update tail (see the marker-loop incident), the Desktop showed:

```
Desktop boot failed: Gateway draining (update_paused). Use hermes gateway status for recovery.
```

But `hermes gateway status` **blocked with no output for >180 s** (measured twice). What actually recovered the system was `hermes gateway restart`.

## Why it blocks

Any `hermes` CLI invocation on an install with venv/lock drift first runs the self-heal dependency sync before doing its work. In the fence/pending state that sync takes minutes, so the very command the error message recommends becomes a hang — from the user's perspective the guidance is "run the command that freezes".

## Suggested improvements

1. In a fence/pending state, make `gateway status` fail fast with the fence reason instead of blocking behind the self-heal.
2. Change the recovery hint from `hermes gateway status` to `hermes gateway restart` (status can't clear anything; restart runs the tail that does).

## Environment

- v0.22.1+73.g4278fec, Windows 11 (Chinese-username home dir), git checkout + PM install
- Incident date: 2026-10-15 (all timestamps below are local +08:00)

## What happened

An `hermes update` failed mid-follow-up: the `dependencies` follow-up died on a half-written `pm/lock.json` (`Unclosed array (at line 128, column 3)`), and `windows_resume` could not verify the gateway relaunch. From then on **every Desktop launch failed with `Gateway draining (update_paused)`**, and a ~77-second loop ran for hours:

```
launch → backend CLI runs the source-update auto-repair ("finishing an interrupted
source update") → the repair writes .hermes-update-in-progress → dies inside
_sync_source_dependencies() ("uv venv failed:" with EMPTY stderr) → dead marker
reclaimed on next launch → next launch re-spawns the repair → repeat (20+ rounds)
```

The gateway itself kept answering `running` on `/api/status` throughout — the fence is **client-side** (`_update_fenced()` in `hermes_cli/gateway_runtime.py:194-221`: live marker OR checkout lock held → `draining(update_paused)`), so the two views coexist and look contradictory.

The loop only ended when a manual `hermes gateway restart` ran the completion tail to success with no Desktop contention.

## Two defects that keep the loop alive

**1. Sync-stage failures never hit the retry counter.**
`_record_completion_attempt(failed=True)` only runs at `hermes_cli/venv_sync.py:545` — after the `source_completion.py` child returns non-zero. A failure inside `_sync_source_dependencies()` (the `uv venv` step, where ours died) exits earlier, so:

- `source-completion-attempts` stays empty forever (no audit trail of the repeated failures)
- the backoff/cap machinery (`COMPLETION_RETRY_BACKOFF_ATTEMPTS=2`, `COMPLETION_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=6` at venv_sync.py:179-214) never engages, so every launch retries

Suggested fix: count an attempt on the sync stage's failure path as well.

**2. Dead-marker reclaim doesn't clear the completion obligation.**
`scripts/desktop-update/marker-claim.ps1:392-397` removes a dead marker when the checkout lock is free, but leaves `source-completion-pending` armed — which is exactly what makes the next launch re-spawn the repair and re-write the marker. Clearing (or re-gating) the pending obligation on reclaim would break the cycle at its fuel source.

## Smaller diagnostic gap from the same incident

`✗ Update failed: venv: uv venv failed:  — retry, or run hermes pm doctor` — the captured stderr was an **empty string** (Chinese-locale Windows; likely a capture/encoding issue). The real uv error never reached the log, making the failure undiagnosable from `update.log` alone.

## Evidence

- `desktop.log`, one loop iteration:
  `16:53:42.754 Resolving Hermes runtime` → marker written `16:53:42.913` (owner pid = the just-spawned backend CLI) → `16:53:44.130 backend using Hermes at ...` → `16:53:46.830 Desktop boot failed: Gateway draining (update_paused)`
- `update.log`: both follow-up failures + the empty-stderr `uv venv failed:` line
- `desktop-update-handoff.log`: `marker-op reclaim: removed a dead update marker` ×20+ across the afternoon
- Recovery: `gateway restart` 16:56 → tail completed → loop gone; a close/reopen cycle later the same evening booted clean in 4s

## Summary

After a live model switch, the chat timeline notice is a **hardcoded English string `'model changed'`** that is (a) **not localized at all** — it stays English in every non-English UI — and (b) **throws away the one piece of information the user actually needs: which model it switched to**. The backend marker contains both the new model and provider; the frontend deliberately discards them and renders a content-free English word.

Version: v0.22.1+33, Windows 11 (source at `ca069e1223`).

## Evidence in source

`apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-messages/hydration.ts`:

```ts
function timelineDisplayContent(message: SessionMessage, content: string): string {
  if (message.display_kind === 'model_switch') {
    return 'model changed'          // ← hardcoded English, no i18n key
  }
  if (message.display_kind === 'auto_continue') {
    return 'resumed interrupted turn'   // ← same problem
  }
  if (message.display_kind === 'personality_switch') {
    return 'personality changed'        // ← same problem
  }
```

- No corresponding key exists in `apps/desktop/src/i18n/en.ts` / `zh.ts` (grep for `model changed` / `modelChanged` returns nothing) — these strings bypass the i18n system entirely.
- Meanwhile the backend pivot marker written by `tui_gateway/server.py` (`_append_model_switch_marker`) contains the full information:

```
[System: model changed to <model> via provider <provider>. From this point forward, ...]
```

The UI has the model name and provider in hand and discards them.

## Why this matters

- The model-switch notice is the **user's audit trail for a runtime change**. "model changed" without naming the model is useless precisely in the situation where accuracy matters most — multi-model setups where the user switched between similar local endpoints (e.g. two quantizations of the same base model on two different machines). Combined with picker checkmark bugs (separate issue), the user is left with **no trustworthy record of which model took over from which point**.
- For non-English users the notice is unreadable noise in an otherwise fully localized UI — a localization hole in a first-party, high-visibility event.
- Same class of problem affects `auto_continue` and `personality_switch` notices.

## Suggested fix

1. Move these strings behind i18n keys and translate them.
2. Parse the model/provider out of the marker (or better: have the gateway put them in `display_metadata`) and render e.g. `Model changed to qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_s · Strata 250` / `模型已切换为 …`.
title: Model-switch timeline notice is a hardcoded English 'model changed' — not localized, and discards the new model/provider the backend already provides

## Summary

**The desktop model picker can permanently lose the ability to show which model is active — zero checkmarks, zero highlighting, across every row, every session, forever — until the user finds an undiscoverable recovery button or manually deletes localStorage keys.** Meanwhile the composer pill keeps showing a model name, so the UI actively *claims* a model is selected while the picker contradicts it. For users running multiple local inference servers (the core Hermes audience), this means **there is no reliable way in the UI to verify which machine/model your messages are actually going to** — a silent misrouting/trust failure, not a cosmetic glitch.

Version: v0.22.1+33, Windows 11 (source at `ca069e1223`).

## Symptoms (all observed together)

1. Model picker list: **no row ever shows the ✓ checkmark or selected background**, including the row that is verifiably current.
2. The composer pill shows a model name (e.g. `Qwen3.8 Flash Next Nvfp4 Nvfp4`) that **contradicts** the picker (no row marked) — the two UI surfaces disagree with each other.
3. Clicking **"Refresh models"** changes nothing (it refetches the catalog but never re-syncs composer state).
4. Opening a **brand-new session** changes nothing — the stale state survives session boundaries.
5. The composer pill itself only refreshes on the next sent message, which makes users think the whole switch failed and send them into a restart loop (app restart does **not** help, because the dirty state lives in Electron localStorage).

## Root cause (traced in source + live data)

The checkmark is computed purely from frontend composer state:

- `apps/desktop/src/lib/model-options.ts` → `catalogProviderMatches()`: current provider must `===` the row's `slug`/`name` or be `in` the row's `aliases`.
- Composer provider/model are persisted in Electron localStorage (`hermes.desktop.composer.provider` / `.model` / `.model-source`). A historical bug (and/or switching between `custom_providers` entries) can leave a **bare `custom`** or otherwise non-canonical value there.
- A bare `custom` is in **no row's alias set** → `catalogProviderMatches` returns false for **every row** → the entire list is permanently uncheckable.
- **There is no self-healing on the frontend.** The backend has exactly this self-heal (bare `custom` falls back to the first entry), and the backend payload is provably correct — I ran the GUI's own data source directly:

```
custom:strata-250-(192.168.3.250:8080) | is_current: True | aliases: ['custom:custom:strata-250-...', 'custom:strata-250-...', 'strata 250 (...)', 'strata-250-...']
custom:strata-5090-(本机:8180)          | is_current: False | aliases: [...]
custom:local-llama.cpp-(8099)           | is_current: False | aliases: [...]
```

So the backend knows exactly which row is current; the frontend throws that truth away and diffs against a dirty localStorage value instead.

- The seeding logic that would re-derive composer state from the profile default **returns early whenever there is an active session**, and `manual` sticky picks take priority over the profile default — so neither a new session nor normal usage ever washes the dirty value. The only in-app recovery is a "reset to saved default" action at the bottom of the picker that most users will never find, and there is no documentation of it.

## Why this is severe

- It is a **silent correctness/visibility failure** for the flagship multi-provider local-inference workflow: the user cannot tell from the UI which endpoint is receiving traffic, and the two UI surfaces (pill vs picker) give contradictory answers.
- It is **sticky and self-perpetuating**: survives app restart, survives new sessions, and the one obvious remedy ("Refresh models") is a dead end — users burn a lot of time restarting apps and re-switching models.
- The failure is **invisible at write time**: whatever wrote the bare `custom` into localStorage did so silently, and nothing ever validates it again.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure 2+ `custom_providers` entries (display names with spaces/parens).
2. Get the composer provider into a non-canonical state (historically: bare `custom` persisted to `hermes.desktop.composer.provider`).
3. Open the model picker → no checkmark on any row, ever.
4. Click "Refresh models" → still nothing. Restart the app → still nothing. Open a new session → still nothing.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Self-heal the composer**: if the persisted provider matches no catalog row (and the catalog is loaded), reseed from the backend's `is_current` row / profile default — mirror the backend's existing bare-`custom` fallback on the frontend.
2. Make **"Refresh models"** also re-validate/re-seed composer state, not just refetch the catalog.
3. Validate on write: never persist a provider string that isn't a canonical slug or known alias.
4. Surface current-selection truth from the backend payload (`is_current`) as a fallback when frontend matching fails, instead of rendering nothing.
