## Summary

A native plugin can correctly propagate `contextvars` into its own background worker and **still** end up with `UnscopedSecretError` under multi-profile hosting, because the context captured during `register(ctx)` is not guaranteed to contain the owning profile's **secret** scope. The plugin manager pins the manager's `HERMES_HOME`, but that alone is not the credential scope.

This should be fixed at the host's plugin lifecycle/spawn boundary rather than requiring every third-party plugin to import `agent.secret_scope` and synthesize its own profile-secret binding.

## Concrete downstream evidence

- [Vocllum/hermes-auto-titler#10](https://github.com/Vocllum/hermes-auto-titler/pull/10) reports 13 failing auto-title calls over 12 hours in a multiplexed deployment. Hook-driven LLM calls succeeded, while retry/sweep calls failed with `UnscopedSecretError` and parked sessions as `blocked`.
- The plugin **already** wraps background workers with `tools.thread_context.propagate_context_to_thread` (and falls back to `contextvars.copy_context`). Its `register(ctx)` calls `start_retry_loop()` which snapshots the registration context. Propagating an unscoped context correctly cannot fix a missing scope at the source.
- The downstream PR patches around this by manually calling `set_secret_scope(build_profile_secret_scope(get_hermes_home()))` immediately before the thread is spawned. This is a workaround, not an appropriate per-plugin contract.

## Host-side source seams to inspect

- `hermes_cli/plugins_loader.py::_plugin_home_scope` sets/resets the Hermes-home override **only**, not the profile secret scope.
- `PluginLoaderMixin._load_plugin_scoped` / `run_with_load_deadline` invokes `register_fn(ctx)` and propagates the caller's context. If the caller has not installed the secret scope, the plugin's own thread inherits none.
- `tools/thread_context.py::propagate_context_to_thread` copies the current context, but cannot add an omitted scope.
- `hermes_cli/web_server.py::start_server` currently activates multi-profile hosting as a *last boot step*. Where plugin discovery happens before activation, background work can snapshot an unscoped context and continue running after multiplex's fail-closed guard becomes active. Please verify this and the launch-profile gateway path with an integration test.

The correct fail-closed behavior in `agent.secret_scope.get_secret` must remain unchanged. No `os.environ` fallback under multiplex should be introduced.

## Expected

Every supported native plugin registration lifecycle has a host-owned, profile-bound runtime context (home + secrets, as appropriate), including when the launch profile is one of multiple served profiles. A plugin using the documented `copy_context` or `propagate_context_to_thread` should not need private `agent.secret_scope` imports. Alternatively, expose a supported `ctx.spawn_thread`/background-worker facility that binds the owning profile, with documented teardown semantics.

## Suggested regression coverage

1. Two-profile gateway/serve with different `.env` keys and one plugin registered per profile.
2. Plugin `register(ctx)` launches a context-propagating worker; after multi-profile activation, the worker's credential read resolves the *owning* profile's key and never another profile's.
3. Launch-profile plugin registered before multiplex activation; worker executes afterward.
4. Existing single-profile and already-profile-scoped registration behavior unchanged.
5. A bare thread without context propagation remains explicitly unsupported (if that is the intended contract), and is not confused with this host registration gap.

## Related, but not duplicates

- [#126737](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/126737) and [#126738](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/126738) ask plugin authors to propagate context from `register(ctx)`. That is necessary, but not sufficient when **the registration context itself** lacks the secret scope.
- [#113746](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/113746), [#115256](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/115256), and [#120310](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/120310) address other individual missing-scope entry points; they don't establish a general plugin background-work contract.
- [#138098](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/138098) covers a specific cron-worker discovery-before-secret-scope ordering issue.

This is based on current source inspection and the downstream reporter's live reproduction, **not** a claim that the full gateway startup matrix has been reproduced independently here.
